entries.name: Discrete Math
entries.description: Use this class of elementary functions to compute discrete math functions for areas such as combinatorics and number theory. The VIs on this palette can return mathematics error codes. Palette Object Description Gcd Computes the greatest common divisor of the input values. Lcm Computes the least common multiple of the input values. Factorial Computes the factorial of n. Prime Factor Computes the prime factorization of an integer. Check Prime Checks whether a number is a prime number. Functions ©

terminals.name: gcd(x,y)
terminals.description: gcd(x,y) returns the greatest common divisor of x and y. gcd(x,y) is the largest divisor common to x and y. Functions 2920 ni.com To compute gcd(x,y), consider the prime factorizations of x and y: x = Πi piai y = Πi pibi where pi are all the prime factors of x and y. If pi does not occur in a factorization, the corresponding exponent is 0. gcd(x,y) then is given by: gcd(x,y) = Πi pimin(ai , bi) For example, the prime factorizations of 12 and 30 are given by: 12 = 2² × 31 × 50 30 = 21 × 31 × 51 s

entries.name: Linear Fit
entries.description: Returns the linear fit of a data set (X, Y) using the Least Square, Least Absolute Residual, or Bisquare method.

terminals.name: Y
terminals.description: Y is the array of dependent values. The length of Y must be greater than or equal to the number of unknown parameters.

terminals.name: X
terminals.description: X is the array of independent values. X must be the same size as Y .

terminals.name: Weight
terminals.description: Weight is the array of weights for the observations ( X , Y ). Weight must be the same size as Y . Weight also must contain non-zero elements. If an element in Weight is less than 0, the VI uses the absolute value of the element. If you do not wire an input to Weight , the VI sets all elements of Weight to 1.

terminals.name: tolerance
terminals.description: tolerance determines when to stop the iterative adjustment of slope and intercept when you use the Least Absolute Residual or Bisquare method. For the Least Absolute Residual method, if the relative difference between residue in two successive iterations is less than tolerance , this VI returns the resulting residue . For the Bisquare method, if any relative difference between slope and intercept in two successive iterations is less than tolerance , this VI returns the resulting slope and intercept .

terminals.name: method
terminals.description: method specifies the fitting method.

terminals.name: parameter bounds

terminals.description: slope max specifies the upper bound for the slope . The default value is Inf , which means no upper bound is imposed on the slope .

terminals.name: intercept min

terminals.name: intercept max
terminals.description: intercept max specifies the upper bound for the intercept . The default value is Inf , which means no upper bound is imposed on the intercept .

terminals.description: Numerator contains the rational polynomial coefficients, in ascending order of power, for the numerator polynomial.

terminals.name: Denominator
terminals.description: Denominator contains the rational polynomial coefficients, in ascending order of power, for the denominator polynomial.

terminals.name: tolerance
terminals.description: tolerance defines a level for multiplicity.

terminals.name: option
terminals.description: option specifies how the VI handles the co-factors of Numerator and Denominator .

terminals.name: Multiplicity
terminals.description: Multiplicity returns the number of times each root in Poles occurs. Multiplicity occurs when the difference between two elements in Poles is less than tolerance .

terminals.name: Polynomial
terminals.description: Polynomial returns the coefficients, in ascending order of power, for the quotient polynomial that results from the division of Numerator by Denominator .

terminals.name: Poles
terminals.description: Poles returns the unique roots of Denominator . The roots of Denominator result from removing all common factors between Numerator and Denominator .

terminals.name: Residues
terminals.description: Residues returns the numerators of the partial fractions that result for each pole.

terminals.name: error
terminals.description: error returns any error or warning from the VI. You can wire error to the Error Cluster From Error Code VI to convert the error code or warning into an error cluster.
